evidence.quote: Mattheus Ramsis Lab Mattheus Ramsis, MD , is an Assistant Professor and Medical Director of Cardiology Informatics at the University of California, San Diego Cardiovascular Institute. He has previously trained in internal medicine at Harvard Medical School-Brigham and Women's Hospital, with subsequent training in cardiovascular disease, trial design, and preventative cardiology at the University of California San Francisco where he served as a clinical instructor. Awards include the National Institutes of Health T-32 award, the Bristol-Myers-Squibb-Foundation Career Development Award, and the American College of Cardiology Executive Board Foundation Award. His previous and ongoing work consists of validating algorithms for remote cardiovascular disease detection, leveraging artificial intelligence to predict disease using electronic health record data, and developing digital biomarkers. He collaborates with multidisciplinary teams of clinicians, researchers, and engineers to leverage data from wearable devices, biomarkers, and electronic health records to create innovative solutions, perform research, and enhance the quality of care. For collaboration opportunities, please contact mramsis@ucsd.edu . Mattheus Ramsis, MD Director, Cardiology Informatics Assistant Professor of Medicine UC San Diego Division of Cardiovascular Medicine
Medical Director of Cardiology Informatics at the University of California, San Diego Cardiovascular Institute.
